title: tdev.tools.v1 design contract (declarative; runtime not implemented)
description: Field syntax is owned here. Architecture section 20 defines transaction, authorization, byte limits and failure semantics. This root validates tool-call fixtures, not raw JSON-RPC.

Revision.description: Unsigned uint64 decimal; reject numeric overflow in the semantic validator.

Path.description: UTF-8 repository-relative path; semantic validator rejects absolute paths, traversal, NUL and control paths. '.' is allowed only for directory/cwd operations.

Ref.description: Additionally validate with git check-ref-format; binding grant required.

signature.description: HMAC-SHA256 of versioned canonical receipt bytes; session secret never enters the sandbox.

env.description: Sandbox-only environment values; reserved credential/control keys rejected semantically. Never inherit native controller environment.

x-tools.name: tdev_context
x-tools.description: Discover authorized repositories/refs and obtain an exact read snapshot. Cached freshness is explicit.

x-tools.name: tdev_read
x-tools.description: Batch bounded file ranges, directories, searches, diffs, status, history and artifacts at one exact target. Item failures and incomplete coverage are explicit.

x-tools.name: tdev_workspace
x-tools.description: Open, compose exact source checkpoints into a new isolated workspace, or close a nonbusy workspace. Compose never mutates its sources.

x-tools.name: tdev_patch
x-tools.description: Atomically apply grouped typed edits to an expected workspace revision. Multiple replacements in one file are sequential inside one staged buffer; the whole group publishes or none does.

x-tools.name: tdev_exec_command
x-tools.description: Execute an arbitrary command only in an authorized credential-free sandbox. Returns an operation handle; completion checkpoints eligible filesystem changes even on nonzero exit. Never re-execute merely because a response was lost.

x-tools.name: tdev_process
x-tools.description: Send sequenced stdin, signal, or request cancellation of an owned operation. Use observe for polling. Unknown input delivery is not automatically retried.

x-tools.name: tdev_validate
x-tools.description: Freeze one exact commit and run the adopted mandatory validation set plus allowed additions. Diagnostic command success is not a validation receipt.

x-tools.name: tdev_integrate
x-tools.description: Publish exactly the commit sealed by the named validation operation using expected-old-head CAS and readback. No implicit recomposition or validation; duplicate receipt effects return the original operation.

x-tools.name: tdev_observe
x-tools.description: Read operation/workspace state and replay logs by byte offset. Does not launch, retry, cancel or publish. Disconnect does not cancel work.

x-semanticChecks: Unique read query IDs; range end >= start; path rules; decoded aggregate byte limits; maxBytes counts actual serialized result content.
Binding/ref grant and exact object membership are checked for every target; handles are not permission.
Process input requires nonempty text or eof=true; input sequence is exact. Signal only exec/validate operations; cancel may target any owned nonterminal operation.
Workspace close refuses busy state. Compose needs same binding/ref and allowed exact source revisions; all-or-nothing conflict checks.
Publication requires current policy and protected exclusive-writer boundary, exact validation receipt, single-parent commit and CAS/readback.
Materialized source types, unresolved LFS/submodules and environment/network presets are capability checked, never silently omitted.
Workspace revision is uint64 decimal; JSON integers must be safe integers. No duplicate JSON object keys or lone surrogates.
Output schemas describe structure; byte/array bounds and ownership remain enforced during generation, not after oversized output is created.
ProcessResult.operation describes the durable control operation; targetOperationId names the exec/validate/integrate operation being controlled. Cancellation acceptance is not proof of termination.
ReadTarget(operationId) accepts artifact queries only. Other read variants require snapshot/workspace. No user-supplied Git object grants access by itself.
Ref list pagination sets refsComplete and refsCursor; ContextInput cursor continuation remains bound to bindingId and authorization.

x-advertisement.input: Inline the input root schema as an object (type:object), then embed only the referenced transitive $defs. Do not duplicate the inlined root definition.
x-advertisement.output: Output schemas are normative and validated server-side, but not advertised in the initial tools/list; avoid repeating the full Operation/receipt schema graph for six tools.
x-advertisement.byteAccounting: Input aggregate bytes and result content budget are checked semantically. Record serialized MCP wire bytes separately, including structuredContent/text duplication.
